Configure schemas, wrappers, and documentation

Source: vignettes/configuration.Rmd
configuration.Rmd

Use one project file to select service files. A service combines local schemas with generation policy. An operation is identified by service ID, HTTP method, and original schema path. Names such as GET /items/{item_id} below must match that path exactly, including trailing slashes.

All project/config/schema paths resolve against the explicit client root, not the current working directory or the service YAML’s directory. Use relative paths inside YAML. Parent traversal, absolute paths, and symlinks are rejected.

Project file: specmill.yml

load_project() and maintenance commands use specmill.yml by default. Pass config explicitly to use a different project filename.

config_version: 1
package: catalogueclient
services: [apis/catalogue.yml]
Field Meaning
config_version Required integer 1
services Required nonempty sequence of distinct service YAML paths
package R package name; read from DESCRIPTION when omitted
formatter Optional {name: air, version: '0.9.0'}; the exact installed version is required
callback_files Optional sequence of development callback source paths to fingerprint, without sourcing them

Use specmill::load_project(root) to validate and inspect the resolved service configuration before generating. Callback names require an explicit environment even for a read-only plan.

Service files 

id: catalogue
schemas:
  files: [schema/catalogue.json]
helper: api_request
selection:
  methods: [GET, POST]
  exclude: ['^/internal/']
documentation: true
policy_version: reviewed-1
Field Meaning
id Required stable service identity, unique in the project
schemas.files Sequence of literal local JSON paths
schemas.patterns Sequence of root-relative file globs; each must match files
schemas.exclude Sequence of case-sensitive regexes matched against schema basenames
helper Required client runtime function name, defined in R/
selection.methods Uppercase methods to include; omitted means all standard HTTP methods
selection.exclude Case-sensitive stringr regexes; exclude an original path if any matches
names Map from METHOD /path to public wrapper name
documentation Boolean; true generates roxygen, help pages, and exports; initialization sets it to true
policy_version Your review/version label, recorded in generation metadata
defaults Operation settings shared across the service
operations Settings keyed by METHOD /original/path
hooks Map from public wrapper name to ordered pre/post hook sequences
hook_config Existing runtime hook YAML path; use this or hooks, never both
hook_callback Client hook executor name; default run_hook
prepare Development callback name; receives and returns an operation, preserving identity
contracts Inline fixed request expectations; see Testing
contracts_file RDS fixed call sequences under tests/testthat/, preserving R classes
response_fixture Default mock response for inline single-call contracts

files and patterns can be combined; paths are deduplicated and sorted. Missing files, unmatched globs, or an empty final schema selection fail. Unknown fields, duplicate explicit keys, invalid types/regexes, executable YAML tags, and name collisions are errors. YAML aliases are supported; explicit keys override merged keys. YAML contains data, never R source strings.

Name and document a wrapper

Add this to the service that selects the catalogue schema:

operations:
  GET /items/{item_id}:
    name: fetch_item
    parameters:
      path item_id: {name: identifier, description: Catalogue item ID.}
      query language: {default: en}
    docs:
      title: Fetch one catalogue item
      description: Retrieve one item in the requested language.
      parameters:
        identifier: The catalogue identifier, for example item-1.
        language: Response language; en or fr.
      return: An R list containing the decoded item response.
      examples:
        - {identifier: item-1}
        - {identifier: item-1, language: fr}
      tags:
        family: catalogue endpoints

Parameter overrides use original location plus name, such as path item_id. Documentation and example inputs use the resulting public R names, such as identifier. Examples are input maps rendered as calls inside dontrun, so a documentation build does not send their requests.

docs supports title, description, parameters, return, examples, tags, and lifecycle. Without overrides, titles/parameter text come from schema metadata and the return text describes the helper response. Improve these for your users: document units, valid IDs, result classes, and service-specific errors.

lifecycle accepts experimental, stable, maturing, superseded, deprecated, defunct, questioning, or soft-deprecated. Install lifecycle in the documentation environment when using badges. Lifecycle is explicit policy; upstream deprecation is not automatic permission to change a wrapper’s lifecycle. Protected lifecycle badges can prevent later regeneration.

tags supports metadata such as family, keywords, seealso, aliases, and client custom tags with existing roxygen handlers. ComptoxR’s apiStage handler remains client code. Executable and structural built-in tags are rejected. Schema descriptions are treated as prose, not executable configuration.

Operation settings

Field Meaning
name Override public R function name; must agree with names if both specify it
helper Override the service helper for this operation
file Output path directly under R/, for example R/catalogue.R
implementation generated (default) or existing, which retains a declared implementation
parameters Schema parameter overrides: name, default, required, exclude, description
extra_parameters Additional public inputs: default, required, type, description
inputs Complete public input map, replacing schema-derived inputs; same fields plus missing_as_null
parameter_order Sequence of public names to place first; remaining parameters follow
request.arguments Named helper arguments built from typed bindings
post_on_skip Boolean, default false; run post-hook after a pre-hook skips the request
post_state parameters (default) or hook_state for the full pre-hook state
docs The documentation policy described above

Per-operation settings merge into defaults. Named maps merge recursively; sequences, a complete inputs map, individual request bindings, and default values replace their corresponding defaults. Keep defaults small enough that you can see the effective behavior of each operation.

A complete inputs map needs request.arguments. Required inputs have no R default and preserve ordinary R argument semantics, including explicitly supplied NULL; the existing helper/hooks own value validation. missing_as_null: true is available only for explicitly required inputs when an existing hook must see omission as NULL. Do not use it merely to silence missing-input errors.

Map public inputs to your existing helper

The default helper contract is:

api_request(method, path, path_params, query, body)

To preserve a different helper interface, explicitly replace its argument map:

operations:
  GET /items/{item_id}:
    name: fetch_item
    inputs:
      identifier: {required: true, type: character}
      verbose: {default: false, type: logical}
    request:
      arguments:
        endpoint: {value: items}
        identifier: {from: [params, identifier]}
        options:
          compact_object:
            verbose: {from: [params, verbose]}

Here the helper must accept endpoint, identifier, and options. Extra inputs are sent only when explicitly bound. Each binding has exactly one form:

Binding Result
{value: items} Literal R data
{from: [params, identifier]} Read a public input
{from: [hook_state, query]} Read pre-hook state; requires a pre-hook
object: {key: <binding>} Named R list, retaining NULL entries
compact_object: {key: <binding>} Named list omitting NULL entries; empty result is list()
array: [<binding>] Unnamed list, preserving positions including NULL
vector: {key: <binding>} Named c() values
{callback: batch_limit} Development callback result: literal data or an R language object

For JSON, use named lists for objects and unnamed lists for arrays, including one-element arrays. NULL, false, zero, and one-element lists are distinct. Do not turn arrays into scalar values for convenience. The helper owns the final serialization and full runtime value validation.

Development callbacks versus runtime hooks

A development binding callback receives one operation while generating source:

callbacks <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
callbacks$batch_limit <- function(operation) {
  quote(as.numeric(Sys.getenv('batch_limit', '1000')))
}
specmill::generate_client(
  root, config = 'specmill.yml', callbacks = callbacks, mode = 'plan'
)

Use {callback: batch_limit} as a request argument binding. A language object such as quote(...) becomes client runtime code; a string remains a quoted literal. A prepare callback instead transforms an operation record and must preserve its identity. These functions run during planning too: keep them deterministic and free of filesystem/network side effects.

Runtime hooks execute when a user calls the generated wrapper:

hook_callback: run_hook
hooks:
  fetch_item:
    pre_request: [validate_identifier]
    post_response: [tidy_item]

The wrapper invokes the client’s executor as run_hook('fetch_item', 'pre_request', list(params = params)). The executor runs the named chain in order and returns state. Returned public parameters replace only those provided by the pre-hook. State can contain skip_request and result. By default, a skipped request returns immediately. Post-hook input normally contains result and params, and the post-hook returns the final wrapper result.

Set post_on_skip: true to run post-processing on a skipped result, or post_state: hook_state to pass the complete pre-hook state with its result replaced. Both require a pre-hook. Hook functions/executor must exist in client runtime source. Unused runtime declarations appear separately in unused_hooks.

Validate the result

After any configuration change, run load_project(), then generate_client(..., mode = 'plan'). Inspect files, drift, diagnostics, mapping_diagnostics, and retained_diagnostics. A client-mapped operation uses your explicit serializer mapping and keeps its original parser limitations visible; it does not acquire native schema support.

Apply only reviewed changes, then run check and the client’s tests.
